caption: SSH Activity
description: SSH Activity events report remote client connections to a server using the Secure Shell (SSH) Protocol.
name: ssh_activity

1.caption: Open
1.description: A new network connection was opened.

3.caption: Reset
3.description: The network connection was abnormally terminated or closed by a middle device like firewalls.

4.caption: Fail
4.description: The network connection failed. For example a connection timeout or no route to host.

5.caption: Refuse
5.description: The network connection was refused. For example an attempt to connect to a server port which is not open.

7.caption: Listen
7.description: A network endpoint began listening for new network connections.

auth_type.description: The SSH authentication type, normalized to the caption of 'auth_type_id'. In the case of 'Other', it is defined by the event source.

auth_type_id.description: The normalized identifier of the SSH authentication type.

3.caption: Host Based
3.description: Authentication based on the client host's identity.

cipher_algorithm.description: The encryption algorithm negotiated for the SSH connection. For example: aes256-gcm@openssh.com or chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com. When the two directions use different algorithms, use the value as reported by the event source.

compression_algorithm.description: The compression algorithm negotiated for the SSH connection. For example: none or zlib@openssh.com.

file.description: The file that is the target of the SSH activity.

host_key_algorithm.description: The public key algorithm of the server host key that the server used to sign the key exchange. For example: ssh-ed25519, rsa-sha2-512 or ecdsa-sha2-nistp256.

host_key_fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the server host key. For example, for a host key fingerprint reported as SHA256: followed by a Base64 digest, set algorithm_id to 3 (SHA-256) and value to the Base64 digest without the SHA256: prefix. A change in the host key presented by the same server can indicate that the server was replaced or that the connection is being intercepted.

kex_algorithm.description: The key exchange algorithm negotiated for the SSH connection. For example: curve25519-sha256 or sntrup761x25519-sha512@openssh.com.

mac_algorithm.description: The message authentication code (MAC) algorithm negotiated for the SSH connection. For example: hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com. When the two directions use different algorithms, use the value as reported by the event source.
